questions.text:
For any discrete random variable X, with probability mass function
[latex]P(X=j)=p_{j}, p_{j}\geq 0, j \in \{0,....N\}[/latex] and [latex] \sum_{j=0}^{N}p_{j}=1[/latex], define the polynomial function [latex]g_{x}(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N}p_{j}z^{j}[/latex]. For a certain discrete random variable Y, there exists a scalar [latex]\beta \in [/latex][0,1] such that [latex]g_{Y}(z)=(1-\beta +\beta z)^{N}[/latex]. The expectation of Y is
questions.solution:
For a pgf, [latex]E[Y]=g_Y'(1)[/latex]:
[latex]g_Y'(z)=N\beta(1-\beta+\beta z)^{N-1}\Rightarrow g_Y'(1)=N\beta[/latex]

(Y is Binomial(N, [latex]\beta[/latex]).)

Answer: [latex]N\beta[/latex]

options: Not expressible in terms of N and [latex]\beta[/latex] alone

questions.text:
Consider the following expression grammar G:
E[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]E-T|T
T[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T+F|F
F[latex]\rightarrow[/latex](E)|id
Which of the following grammars is not left recursive, but is equivalent to G?
questions.solution:
Remove left recursion with the standard rule [latex]A\rightarrow A\alpha\mid\beta\Rightarrow A\rightarrow\beta A',\ A'\rightarrow\alpha A'\mid\epsilon[/latex]:
- [latex]E\rightarrow E-T\mid T[/latex] becomes [latex]E\rightarrow TX,\ X\rightarrow-TX\mid\epsilon[/latex]
- [latex]T\rightarrow T+F\mid F[/latex] becomes [latex]T\rightarrow FY,\ Y\rightarrow+FY\mid\epsilon[/latex]

Option 1 is still left recursive, option 2 keeps [latex]T\rightarrow T+F[/latex] and loses the minus, option 4 changes the language.

Answer: Option 3

questions.text:
A system shares 9 tape drives. The current allocation and maximum requirement of tape drives for three processes are shown below:

Which of the following best describes current state of the system ?
questions.solution:
Allocated = 3 + 1 + 3 = 7, so 2 drives are free. Remaining needs: P1 4, P2 5, P3 2.
P3 can finish (needs 2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] free 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P1 can finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] free 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P2 can finish. A safe sequence exists, and no process is stuck right now.

Answer: Safe, Not Deadlocked

questions.text:
Consider a binary code that consists of only four valid code words as given below:
00000,01011,10101,11110
Let the minimum Hamming distance of the code be p and the maximum number of erroneous bits that can be corrected by the code be q. Then the values of p and q are
questions.solution:
Pairwise distances: 00000-01011 = 3, 00000-10101 = 3, 00000-11110 = 4, 01011-10101 = 4, 01011-11110 = 3, 10101-11110 = 3.

Minimum p = 3. It can correct [latex]\lfloor(3-1)/2\rfloor=1[/latex] error.

Answer: p = 3 and q = 1

questions.text:
Consider two hosts X and Y, connected by a single direct link of rate [latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits/sec . The
distance between the two hosts is 10,000 km and the propagation speed along the link is
2x[latex]10^{8}[/latex] m/sec . Host X sends a file of 50,000 bytes as one large message to host Y
continuously. Let the transmission and propagation delays be p milliseconds and q
milliseconds, respectively . Then the values of p and q are
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Transmission: [latex]\frac{50000\times8}{10^6}=0.4[/latex] s = 400 ms
- Propagation: [latex]\frac{10^7}{2\times10^8}=0.05[/latex] s = 50 ms

Answer: p = 400 and q = 50
